title: U.S. House · Georgia's 14th District
area: Northwest Georgia, including Rome, Dalton, and Cartersville.

context.text: Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R) withdrew from the Republican primary for this seat and left Congress in early 2026; a special election was held to fill the vacancy. Clayton Fuller (R) won the special general runoff election on April 7, 2026 and took office on April 14, 2026. He then won the May 19, 2026 regular Republican primary and is the incumbent on the November ballot.
Cook Political Report rates the November general election Solid Republican; Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball also rate it Safe/Solid Republican.

Andrew Underwood (Libertarian), whom Ballotpedia lists as withdrawn or disqualified, does not appear on the printed U.S. House District 14 contest on the Paulding County Nov. 3, 2026 composite sample ballot (Clay Fuller and Shawn Harris) or on the Georgia Secretary of State's Sept. 15, 2026 list of certified write-in candidates.

candidates.name: Clayton Fuller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the special general runoff election on April 7, 2026, then won the May 19, 2026 regular Republican primary

summary.text: Clayton Fuller is a U.S. Air Force veteran, former prosecutor, and former White House Fellow who won the special election to succeed Marjorie Taylor Greene in April 2026. He holds degrees from Emory University, Cornell University, and Southern Methodist University's law school.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in English from Emory University (2004), a Master of Public Administration from Cornell University (2006), and a J.D. from Southern Methodist University's Dedman School of Law (2009); later earned a master's degree in military arts and sciences from the Air Command and Staff College (2020).
Has served in the U.S. Air Force since 2009; career experience includes serving as a staff judge advocate and as a district attorney with the Lookout Mountain Judicial Circuit in Georgia.
Served as a White House Fellow, working in counter-terrorism between the White House and the Pentagon.
Won the special general election runoff for Georgia's 14th District on April 7, 2026, defeating Shawn Harris, and took office on April 14, 2026.

priorities.text: In a 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, described himself as a "Christian Conservative who will defend the unborn, support the 2nd Amendment, and fight illegal immigration."
Said he is "passionate about bringing prosperity and growth to small towns in North Georgia" and about reducing the national debt.

positions.summary: Campaign website, under the heading "Mass Deportation Now," says he supports efforts to remove immigrants who are in the country without permission.
positions.quote: Clay supports all efforts to empower the Trump Administration as they seek to remove the millions of illegal immigrants who do not have permission to be in this country.

record.text: Won the special general election runoff for Georgia's 14th Congressional District, 55.9% to 44.1%, on April 7, 2026, and took the oath of office on April 14, 2026.

candidates.name: Shawn Harris
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary; also the Democratic nominee in the March–April 2026 special election for this seat

summary.text: Shawn Harris is a U.S. Marine Corps and Army veteran and Democratic nominee who ran against Marjorie Taylor Greene in 2024 and against Clayton Fuller in both the 2026 special election and the regular general election.

background.text: Born in Blakely, Georgia; served in the U.S. Marine Corps and the U.S. Army.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Tuskegee University and a graduate degree from the Army War College.
Was the Democratic nominee against incumbent Marjorie Taylor Greene in the 2024 general election, losing 64.4% to 35.6%.
Ran in the 2026 special election for the vacant seat, finishing first in the March 10 special general election and losing the April 7 runoff to Clayton Fuller, 55.9% to 44.1%.

priorities.text: Says he would publicly list every bill on his website in everyday language with how he intends to vote and why, and hold monthly town halls with no screened questions.
Says his priority in Washington is making sure working people in Georgia can build a good life, and proposes policies on housing costs, gas prices, and grocery prices.
Says real healthcare reform means protecting and expanding local medical infrastructure and bringing more healthcare providers to Northwest Georgia.

positions.summary: Campaign website lists expanding Medicare to include nursing homes for long-term care, alongside defending Medicaid and Medicare.
positions.quote: Expand Medicare to include nursing homes for long-term care.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he supports the Women's Health Protection Act, which he describes as establishing a nationwide right to provide and receive abortion care.
positions.quote: This legislation establishes a nationwide right to provide and receive abortion care. This is a health care issue, and the decision belongs between a woman and her doctor — not politicians.

positions.summary: Campaign website proposes scrapping the Social Security payroll tax cap so high earners continue paying into the system through the year.
positions.quote: Set the rules fairly, so all Americans pay the same rate for the same guarantee, by scrapping the payroll tax cap.

statements.quote: I have no interest in taking anyone’s gun. What I want is for gun owners to be responsible — trained on the firearms they own, and storing them safely.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements from his campaign issue pages (shawnharrisforcongress.com). Some pages carry no date; the site also lists 2026 media interviews whose text was not reviewed. The site does not state positions on immigration, tariffs, or most other tracked issues.

candidates.name: Rob Ruszkowski

summary.text: Rob Ruszkowski is an independent candidate for Georgia's 14th Congressional District and a certified write-in candidate: his name is on the Georgia Secretary of State's list of certified write-in candidates for U.S. House District 14 and is not printed on the ballot. He founded Hi-Tech Paging Inc. in Atlanta in 1991.

background.text: Earned a finance degree from Hofstra University; founded Hi-Tech Paging Inc. in Atlanta in 1991 and grew it to five locations in Gwinnett County, Georgia.

priorities.text: Says he is running to establish a "Human Rights Bill" guaranteeing clean air and water, a living wage, fair healthcare, equal justice, and the right to build a secure future.
Says he would fight to "end dark-money influence, protect voting rights, and rebuild a government that works for everyday Americans."

positions.summary: Ballotpedia survey response says he would use House revenue powers to end tax loopholes that benefit corporations and billionaires.
positions.quote: End tax loopholes and special-interest giveaways that allow corporations and billionaires to hoard wealth while our communities fight rising costs.

statements.quote: establishing a new Human Rights Bill that guarantees clean air and water, a living wage, fair healthcare, equal justice, and the right to build a secure future
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response

statements.quote: I’m committed to rural revitalization, renewable energy independence, strengthening democracy
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response

candidates.researchNotes: Statements from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026). No campaign website found. Ballotpedia lists him as an independent write-in candidate. Survey does not directly address most tracked issues.
candidates.ballotNote: Certified write-in candidate (not printed on the ballot)
